articleTitle: High Current Density and High Breakdown Voltage Enhancement-Mode Gate-Controlled Heterojunction Vertical β-Ga2O3 MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel high-performance enhancement- mode (E-mode) gate-controlled heterojunction β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> vertical power MOSFET (GCH-VMOS) has been proposed and investigated using Sentaurus TCAD simulation. At V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf> = 0 V, both the p-type NiO and the metal–insulator– semiconductor (MIS) trench gate structure depletes the conduction channel to realize the E-mode. Furtherly, in the forward blocking state V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> > 0 V, the gate-controlled NiO/β- Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> heterojunction is reverse biased and enhances the pinch- off effect to obtain a low leakage current and thus high breakdown voltage (BV). In the on-state V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf> > 0 V, the NiO/β- Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> heterojunction is forward biased, and the depletion region shrinks and the channel conduction area increases to achieve high current density. The simulated results showed a positive threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>) of 0.6 V, a low specific on- resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on,sp</inf>) of 4.26 mΩ·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, a high current density of 1.5 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, a high BV of 2559 V (at V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf> = 0 V) and power figure of merit (PFOM) up to 1.54 GW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for the GCH-VMOS. The proposed E-mode device demonstrates great potential for the next generation of power electronics.

articleTitle: Ku-Band High-Efficiency Broadband MMIC Poawer Amplifier in 0.25-$\mu \mathrm{m}$ GaAs pHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14 - 17.5\text{GHz}$</tex> high-efficiency broadband monolithic microwave integrated circuit(MMIC) high-power amplifier (HPA) is designed in this article using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.25 - \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> GaAs pHEMT technology. The article describes the design process of this PA. The input matching network uses a high-order high-pass structure(HHS) to suppress low-frequency signal gain to achieve gain flattening. The inter-stage matching network is designed with virtual bias lines(VBL) to maintain structural symmetry, which can increase bandwidth while reducing loss. The maximum output power of the designed HPA is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35\text{dBm}({3{\mathrm{\ W}}})$</tex> when the drain voltage is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5{\mathrm{\ V}}$</tex> and the gate voltage is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$- 0.8{\mathrm{\ V}}$</tex>. The small signal and power gains are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20.8{\mathrm{\ dB}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20.5{\mathrm{\ dB}}$</tex> respectively, and its flatness is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5{\mathrm{\ dB}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.4{\mathrm{\ dB}}$</tex> respectively. It also achieves a PAE of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$36{\mathrm{\% }}$</tex> in the frequency range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14 - 17.5\text{GHz}$</tex>.

articleTitle: More than Circadian Regulation: A Brief Review of Blue Light Treatment of Infections and Cancers
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: What light can do is more than illumination. As a more specific case, what blue light can do is more than circadian regulation, which has been one of the most representative cases of more-than-illumination applications. In its role of regulating circadian rhythm, blue light suppresses melatonin by stimulating the ganglion cells in human retina. Unlike this, other therapeutic modalities of blue light are mainly linked with the reactive oxygen species (ROS) induced by blue light. ROS can further induce cytotoxicity, or trigger signaling pathways that can lead to the death of pathogenic cells. Therefore, one main direction is anti-microbial blue light therapy to treat infectious diseases, caused by various microbes, such as bacteria, fungi and viruses. Likewise, the oxidative stress induced by blue light has also been utilized in killing cancer cells, and has shown its effectiveness in treating cancers. Another new direction is the so-called suppressing EMT (epithelial mesenchymal transition) blue light (SEBL) therapy to treat the fibrosis and migration of cancer cells, where ROS plays an important role in downregulating the concentration of the translational growth factor, TGF-β1, which controls the EMT process of cancer cells. This brief review aims at introducing the newly emerging therapeutic potentials of blue light in treating these diseases, with the focus on the link between blue light and ROS together with its downstream pathways.

articleTitle: Study on the Resistivity and Porosity of Nano Copper Powder Under Low-Temperature Sintering without Pressure
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Copper powders with an average particle size of 300 nm were prepared by ascorbic acid reduction using methionine as a protective agent and further mixed with ethylene glycol to make a copper paste for pressureless low-temperature sintering. The sintering properties of copper paste were tested using SEM, XRD, TG, and four-probe tester, and the changes of resistivity and porosity at different sintering temperatures and sintering times were investigated, and the sintering behavior was analyzed by microstructure transformation. The results show that the resistivity can be as low as 17.7 µΩ-cm, the sintering temperature reaches 250℃ to form the initial sintering neck, the resistivity is around 50 µΩ-cm, which can be satisfied with the application, and the porosity increases with the increase of the sintering neck.

articleTitle: Heteroepitaxial MoS2 on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: As a typical two-dimensional (2D) material, molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) can be used in micro-nano electronics, optoelectronics and flexible wearable devices due to its adjustable bandgap width, high electron mobility and excellent mechanical properties. Wide bandgap semiconductors (WBS) have the advantages of high breakdown voltage, electron mobility and thermal conductivity. Their good lattice matching makes WBS an excellent substrate material for MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The performance of devices based on MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/WBS heterostructure is highly dependent on the quality of epitaxial MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. This review discusses the preparation methods of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on silicon carbide (SiC), gallium nitride (GaN), gallium oxide (Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and diamond in recent years. In addition to the common exfoliation method and transfer method, people can now directly epitaxially grow high-quality MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films on WBS substrates through chemical vapor deposition (CVD), pulsed laser deposition (PLD), and sulfurization of metallic molybdenum (Mo) methods. Devices fabricated based on these methods such as photodetectors, tunnel diodes, and gas sensors are also discussed. Finally, the challenges and future directions of epitaxial MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on WBS are pointed out.

articleTitle: Based on 0.15μm GaAs Process X-Band Low Power Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, an 8∼12 GHz low power and low noise amplifier based on 0.15 μm GaAs pHEMT process is introduced. The two-stage amplifier is composed of two common source transistor cascades. The pre-stage amplifier mainly realizes minimum noise matching, and the post-stage amplifier mainly realizes power gain matching, and the RLC negative feedback network is added to effectively improve the small-signal gain flatness. Based on self-bias technology and current multiplexing method, the amplifier can improve the gain while greatly reducing the power consumption. EM simulation results show that in the 8∼12 GHz frequency band, the gain of the amplifier is better than 20 dB, the gain flatness is ±0.3 dB, the return loss of the input and output is better than 12 dB and 15 dB respectively, the typical noise coefficient in the band is 1.05 dB, the DC power consumption is only 65mW, and the chip size is 1.4 × 1.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The chip has excellent low noise performance and high linearity characteristics with low power consumption and small size, which is suitable for satellite communication and radar applications. At the same time, the RF performance before and after adding RLC negative feedback network and the change of chip noise coefficient under different bias are investigated. The results show that the gain flatness can be significantly improved after adding RLC negative feedback network, and the input reflection is slightly deteriorated. In the range of 2.5-5 V bias voltage, the typical noise coefficient of the chip is less than 1.12 dB in the frequency band, and it has good stability.

articleTitle: Optimization of 1700V 4H-SiC Semi-Superjunction Schottky Diode with Multi-Step Trenched Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: A novel 1700 V 4H-SiC semi-superjunction(SJ) Schottky diode have been designed and simulated in this study to alleviat the tradeoff dilemma between specific on resistance and blocking voltage in SiC power devices. The proposed multi-step trenched structure could be realized by the self- aligned process, and the p-pillars are then formed through vertical implantation into the bottom of the trenches. This practical and cost-effective fabrication method ensures controllable trench morphology and uniform p-doping below each level of trenches. Composed of a 4 μm SJ region above a 6 μm drift region, the optimized SiC semi-SJ have achieved a breakdown voltage above 2000 V with a specific on- resistance as low as 0.997 mΩ·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which breaks the theoretical 1-D limit of the SiC unipolar device. Furthermore, the proposed semi-SJ widens the implantation window by 37.5% compared to full-SJ, while realizing one order of magnitude lower leakage current due to the decreased surface electric field.

articleTitle: Characterization, Analysis, and Failure Investigation of SiC Materials and Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: SiC materials and devices are highly regarded in the power semiconductor industry for their exceptional electrical, thermal, and chemical properties. They meet the demanding requirements of high temperature, voltage, frequency, power, and radiation resistance applications. With the increasing demand for new energy vehicles, 5G communications, rail transit, and ultra-high voltage transmission, SiC power devices are rapidly expanding. However, the quality of SiC wafers still needs improvement compared to well-established Si-based semiconductor technology. The maturity of SiC wafer manufacturing directly impacts device performance. This comprehensive review focuses on the thorough characterization and analysis of SiC wafers. It includes quantitative and qualitative assessments of material composition, trace elements, microscopic and lattice structures, binding energy, chemical bonds, and electrical properties. SiC wafers and epitaxial layers have defect densities several orders of magnitude higher than Si wafers, significantly affecting the electrical performance and reliability of semiconductor devices. The study analyzes surface defects in SiC wafers and calculates yield using a Poisson Model based on defect density, providing insights for SiC manufacturing cost analysis. Additionally, the review conducts a series of systematic failure investigations on a SiC power trench MOSFET through failure mode analysis. Thermally-induced voltage variation technology identifies the failure location. Electrical performance simulation analysis utilizes physical parameters extracted from a matured SiC MOSFET product chip. This report offers a comprehensive overview of SiC material and device characterization, analysis, and failure investigation for power electronics engineering. The findings enhance the understanding of SiC technology and its potential for further advancements in the power semiconductor industry.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation method for UV LEDs
publicationTitle: 2023 20th China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2023 9th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Compared to traditional mercury UV-light sources, ultraviolet light-emitting diodes (UV LEDs) as a new solid-state ultraviolet light source, has been applied in fields such as disinfection, medical diagnosis, phototherapy, solidification, detection, and sensing due to its many advantages. At present, ultraviolet LED technology has achieved rapid development, in order to predict the lifetime of UV LEDs quickly, analyzing the failure mechanism of UV LEDs and selecting suitable lifetime prediction programmes are of significance importance for improving reliability. Therefore, this article focuses on the accelerated life testing (ALT) and accelerated degradation testing (ADT) based on UV LEDs, summarizes the lifetime prediction methods reported in domestic and foreign literature, introduces the principles and applicable scenarios of different lifetime prediction methods.his article summarizes the lifetime prediction methods of ultraviolet LEDs, and provides reference for the reliability research of UV LEDs.
